newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cyclone watch lifted over Cocos Islands.
newsitem.headline: Australia cyclone watch lifted over Cocos Islands.

text.p: A cyclone watch for the Australian territory of the Cocos Islands in the Indian Ocean has been cancelled, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Tuesday.
At 1000 GMT cyclone Rhonda was estimated to be 360 km west southwest of the Cocos islands and moving southeast at 12 km an hour, the bureau said.
The cyclone was unlikely to pose any immediate threats to oil and gas projects operating offshore Western Australia, a spokesman for Woodside Petroleum Ltd said.
"Rhonda is so far away it really poses no dramas," he said.

Woodside is an equal partner in the Wanaea-Cossack field on Western Australia's North West shelf with The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, Chevron Corp and the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
The bureau maintained its category two rating for the the cylcone, with maximum wind gusts of 165 km an hour near the centre.
It is expected to track south of the islands, though winds there will be strong at times over the next 24 hours to 36 hours, the bureau said.
